stories.title: AI company behind micro data center plan in Concord says its design is ‘the way of the future'
stories.summary: A new micro data center in Concord could be one of the first of its kind, using immersion cooling and repurposed heat to warm sidewalks and greenhouses instead of wasting water and power. The company behind it says this sustainable design is 'the way of the future.'
stories.extended_summary: Instead of guzzling water and roaring like a jet engine, the micro data center planned for East Concord would recycle its own heat to warm winter sidewalks and greenhouses. Levitate Inc. CEO Ryan Howard says the closed-loop immersion cooling system is a direct response to the excesses of hyperscale data centers — and he hopes to break ground before the end of the year. It's one of three pilot projects nationwide, including a converted sugar plant in Montana and a plum farm in Washington.

stories.title: This Louisiana founder is building tools to help rural hospitals stay open
stories.summary: After 25 years in medical billing, single mother Nicole Oliver founded Medvient to help rural hospitals stay afloat. Her tool Recon flags underpayments and denials in about a minute — and it's already in pilot programs as dozens of Louisiana hospitals face closure.
stories.extended_summary: Nicole Oliver spent 25 years watching small billing problems snowball before anyone noticed — so she built a tool that catches them in about a minute. Her startup Medvient's first product, Recon, uploads a year of insurance claims and instantly flags underpayments, repeated denials, and overdue payments, then hands billing staff a prioritized action plan. With 43% of Louisiana's rural inpatient hospitals at risk of closing, that kind of speed could be the difference between staying open and shutting down.
